recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any future adjustment to the strength or detailed semantics of DocumentReference _content search should be handled through the later FHIR-54535 work-group process, not by altering this already-applied R5 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-20417 was a Published FHIR-core DocumentReference change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking to clarify use of the generic _content search parameter for free-text discovery of DocumentReference content. The resolution clarified that a server declaring _content support on DocumentReference agrees to search content included in DocumentReference.content.attachment.data and DocumentReference.content.attachment.url.
initial_application: Commit 3c56ef94e5762b202503cc4224a9941ac9522dfe added an implementation note for FHIR-20417 to source/documentreference/documentreference-notes.xml. Later commit 97cf6bb0ede5497d006a53d90f53c1cc2b41248f corrected the path to DocumentReference.content.attachment.url and added code markup, leaving the approved rule in place.
additional_context: DocumentReference is active in source/fhir.ini, so its notes page is in current build scope. The 2019 Zulip thread that led to GF/FHIR-20417 supports clarifying generic _content/_text behavior for attachment bits. OO minutes on 2020-07-16 record the DocumentReference block vote with no pulls and 8-0-5 approval. Later FHIR-54535 and a 2025 Zulip conformance discussion question whether the current SHALL needs R6 clarification, but FHIR-54535 is Triaged/Unresolved and does not supersede FHIR-20417.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current active note says that _content shall search across DocumentReference.content.attachment.data and DocumentReference.content.attachment.url, which satisfies the published FHIR-20417 resolution.

related_jiras.note: Unresolved/Triaged R6 request for clarifying whether DocumentReference _content searches base64, decoded attachment content, URL text, or URL target content. It is background only for this seed.
The same historical implementation commit also addressed a separate DocumentReference generated-operation issue, but that operation change is outside FHIR-20417.
